samples.summary: No design doc update accompanies this behavioral change, despite repo precedent. CONTRIBUTING.md:13-14/58-60 requires writing or updating a doc under docs/design/ for a non-trivial change, and the immediately preceding sibling work on the same feature (#66, docs/tasks/active/20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md step 6) explicitly ended with "Note the endpoint affinity in docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md". This PR extends affinity production to four hit-test sites plus getWrapAffinity across table cells and header/footer regions, but leaves the canonical `lineAffinity` prose in docs-local-caret-anchoring.md (API Boundary, lines 80-94) untouched — the doc still reads as if only body-block hit-tests and selection.ts participate. The task note (docs/tasks/active/20260822-docs-cell-hf-wrap-affinity-todo.md) has no design-doc step at all.
samples.evidence: docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:89 "`selection.ts` passes the endpoint affinity into `findPageForPosition` (and `resolvePositionPixel` for cell-internal selections)" — the source of cell-internal endpoint affinity introduced here is not recorded anywhere in docs/design.

samples.summary: The getWrapAffinity half of the issue is only partially fixed: blocks inside a *nested* table cell still can never report 'forward'. getVisualLineRange's cell branch resolves `cellInfo.tableBlockId` against `layout.blocks` (top-level layout blocks only), so for a block inside a table nested in a cell the lookup misses, the fall-through `layout.blocks.find(pos.blockId)` also misses, and the function returns `[0, 0]` — making getWrapAffinity (line 4142) answer 'backward' unconditionally. The issue note states the defect as "cell-inner and header/footer blocks fall through to 'backward' after typing wraps a line", and the hit-test half of this PR was deliberately extended to arbitrary nesting depth via resolveOffsetInNestedTable, so the typing path is now inconsistent with the click path at depth ≥ 2.
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:4058 `const tableLb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cellInfo.tableBlockId);` — nested table blocks are not members of `layout.blocks`; contrast resolveOffsetInNestedTable (line 4901) which the PR does thread affinity through.

samples.summary: getWrapAffinity re-implements the boundary rule inline instead of delegating to the new shared helper, which undercuts the stated purpose of extracting `hitTestLineAffinity` ("single source of the rule", per the task note step for find-position-at-pixel). `return hitTestLineAffinity(pos.offset, start, start === 0)` would express the same thing and keep one definition of the rule; as written there are now two spellings of it in the package (visual-line.ts:25 and here), which can drift.
samples.evidence: text-editor.ts:4142 `return start === pos.offset && start > 0 ? 'forward' : 'backward';` vs visual-line.ts:25 `return !isFirstLineOfBlock && offset === lineStartOffset ? 'forward' : 'backward';`

verdict.reason: The canonical design doc already records the contract this change conforms to, and the repo's doc obligation is conditioned on architecture/data-model changes, which this is not. docs/design/docs/docs-local-caret-anchoring.md:73-94 documents `lineAffinity` on `DocPosition` (:76), states it region-agnostically as view-level metadata (:80-87), and explicitly names the cell-internal path the finding calls unrecorded: "`selection.ts` passes the endpoint affinity into `findPageForPosition` (and `resolvePositionPixel` for cell-internal selections)" (:89-91); the doc is already scoped to body/header/footer/table-cell blocks (:52) with dedicated Headers-And-Footers (:243-248) and Tables (:250-258) sections. No sentence in it claims only body hit-tests produce affinity, so this change makes the implementation conform to already-documented prose rather than invalidating it. The diff itself adds no architecture or data-model surface: a 3-arg pure helper (packages/docs/src/view/visual-line.ts:20-24) that find-position-at-pixel.ts:117-118 and text-editor.ts:4437-4438,4549 delegate to; `DocPosition.lineAffinity` predates it. CONTRIBUTING.md:11-12 and :44-51 route bug fixes straight to a PR, and :57-61 limits the design-doc requirement to "Architecture / data-model changes"; CLAUDE.md:58-63 repeats the split ("Architecture changes go to docs/design/") and requires the task pair, which exists (docs/tasks/active/20260822-docs-cell-hf-wrap-affinity-todo.md + -lessons.md). The claimed precedent also does not hold: #66 had a doc step because it added the field to `DocPosition` (20260822-selection-line-affinity-todo.md:30-34,57-58), while the immediately preceding sibling #931 threaded the same affinity through getVisualLineRange/Start/End including the table-cell branch (20260822-docs-visual-line-affinity-todo.md:32-56) with no doc step and no resulting design-doc mention anywhere. At most this is a "also list the producers" documentation preference — minor by kind, non-blocking.

finding.evidence: text-editor.ts:4058 `const tableLb = layout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cellInfo.tableBlockId);` — nested table blocks are not members of `layout.blocks`; contrast resolveOffsetInNestedTable (line 4901) which the PR does thread affinity through.

verdict.reason: Verified in-repo. text-editor.ts:4058 resolves `cellInfo.tableBlockId` against `layout.blocks`, but getCellInfo (3134-3139) returns the *immediate* parent table from blockParentMap (nesting chain must be walked, cf. range-slices.ts:80-92), and layout.blocks contains only top-level blocks (layout.ts:361-456; nested tables appear only as a `nestedTable` synthetic line, table-layout.ts:75-81). So for a block inside a nested table cell, tableLb is undefined, the fall-through find at 4091 also misses, [0,0] is returned at 4092, and getWrapAffinity (4140-4143) can only answer 'backward'. Nested tables are reachable/supported (document.ts:750 insertTableInCell), and no guard prevents the path. The hit-test half of the same task does thread affinity through arbitrary depth (resolveOffsetInNestedTable, 4879-5008, affinity at 5006-5008/4869/4876), while the task doc frames both as one deliverable ("cell-inner … fall through to 'backward' after typing wraps a line", 20260822-docs-cell-hf-wrap-affinity-todo.md:15-17, steps 51-60) with no non-goal excluding nesting. That is an unmet acceptance criterion / inconsistent-fit issue in the design-fit lane: major.
